<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
2. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
3. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system deletes everything under
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then re-runs the experiment in your
repaired workspace as a foreground process, using the launch script:

```text
tool_schema/alfworld_case/train.sh
```

with this environment:

```text
RUN_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
```

`train.sh` takes no positional arguments and reads four authorized, idle GPUs
from `N_GPUS=4` / `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`. The effective run uses:

- model `/workspace/tool_schema/Qwen3-4B`
- train data `/workspace/tool_schema/datasets/alfworld/difficulty-v1-s42/train.parquet`
- validation data `/workspace/tool_schema/datasets/alfworld/balanced1008-s42/validation.parquet`
- the fixed budget baked into `train.sh`: `trainer.total_training_steps=63`
  and `trainer.test_freq=20` (eval at steps 0, 20, 40, 60, 63)
- `WANDB_MODE=offline`, `WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`

`train.sh` writes `train.log`, `validation/`, `rollouts/`, and offline W&B
under `RUN_DIR`. A task-specific grading script then reads **only this fresh
run's** files under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` and scores the key
metrics; logs written anywhere else are ignored. Make sure your repaired
workspace still runs correctly under these exact settings. Do not copy, edit,
or fabricate log metrics. Otherwise the run is scored 0.
I’ll inspect the staged run and held-out results, trace any failure to the code or configuration, and write the repair report at `/workspace/report.md`. I’ll only run non-training checks.

Overall success rose from 22/96 to 30/96, entirely in other task families. I’ll fix name resolution at the executor boundary and add regression checks; the evidence does not justify changing the training settings.

*** Add File: /workspace/report.md
+The staged experiment is **unhealthy**: it completes training and improves on some tasks, but a tool-schema/executor mismatch prevents cleaning, heating, and cooling actions from executing. Those three task families remain at zero held-out success throughout the run. The repair resolves advertised names to native executor names before validating and executing the call.
+
+1. **Root cause and evidence**
+
+   In `tool_schema/alfworld_case/tools.py`, `SCHEMA_NAMES` advertises `clean_object`, `heat_object`, and `cool_object`, while `REGISTRY` contains `clean`, `heat`, and `cool`. Before this repair, `command_for()` looked up the advertised name directly in `REGISTRY` and raised `ToolCallError("unknown_tool")`. `Episode.act()` in `episode.py` catches that exception before `env.step()`, returns “The environment state did not change,” and still consumes an episode turn. Both training and validation use this path through `TrajectoryAgentFlow`, selected by `alfworld_schema.yaml`.
+
+   This is directly observable, rather than inferred from an unusual configuration. In `results/baseline63/validation/0.jsonl`, line 12, task `trial_T20190906_201106_979461`, the model takes `soapbar 1`, moves to `sinkbasin 1`, then calls `clean_object` with the correct `object` and `receptacle` fields. The call receives `unknown_tool`. Placing the uncleaned soapbar on the toilet does not win; the episode reaches 40 turns with score 0. The same task fails at the same dispatch boundary in `validation/63.jsonl`, line 12. A direct pre-repair check reproduced `unknown_tool` for all three advertised names.
+
+   All five frozen validation files contain the same 96 unique held-out tasks: 48 seen and 48 unseen, with eight tasks per family in each split. Scores agree with the nested environment-success flags. Aggregation must use `steps[-1].task_family`, `steps[-1].split`, and `steps[-1].num_steps`; the top-level `num_steps=1` denotes one packed training trajectory, not one environment action.
+
+   | Evaluation step | Seen success | Unseen success | Combined success | Clean / heat / cool successes, each out of 16 | Episodes at 40 turns |
+   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+   | 0 | 11/48 | 11/48 | 22/96 (22.92%) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 74/96 |
+   | 20 | 12/48 | 13/48 | 25/96 (26.04%) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 71/96 |
+   | 40 | 13/48 | 14/48 | 27/96 (28.12%) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 69/96 |
+   | 60 | 13/48 | 16/48 | 29/96 (30.21%) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 67/96 |
+   | 63 | 14/48 | 16/48 | 30/96 (31.25%) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 66/96 |
+
+   Across these validation files, 191 well-formed treatment calls followed by recorded feedback received `unknown_tool`: 114 cleaning, 37 heating, and 40 cooling calls. The saved training rollouts at steps 1, 32, and 63 contain another 146 such failures. Counts use the response field once per episode and require a following tool response; terminal feedback is not always included in the text dump. No native `clean`, `heat`, or `cool` calls appear in these saved outputs. At step 63, successes are confined to simple placement (14/16), two-object placement (13/16), and light inspection (3/16).
+
+   The reward and optimization path explains why training does not repair the dispatch defect. `recipes/alfworld/reward_fn.py` scores actual environment success; preprocessing sets ground truth to `{"success": null}`, so runtime success determines the reward. Saved scores match those success flags. Every treatment-family training rollout in the three available dumps has reward zero. The four completions per prompt therefore provide no within-group outcome variation for those tasks: `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage()` in `agent_r1/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py` subtracts the group mean, yielding zero policy-gradient advantage for all-zero groups. Only 2/16, 1/16, and 1/16 prompt groups have mixed outcomes in the respective dumps. Increasing training reward elsewhere does not establish health for these held-out families.
+
+   I also checked other possible explanations against `results/baseline63/train.log`, its frozen Hydra configuration, launch code, and trajectory processing:
+
+   - The run completes 63/63 steps in about 2 hours 19 minutes, with all five evaluations. Mean training-step time is 106.77 seconds, including 74.53 seconds of generation and 21.32 seconds of actor update. Tool-parser errors occur, but there is no fatal training traceback or out-of-memory failure in the log.
+   - Training prompt clipping, response clipping, and aborted-response ratios are all zero. The largest recorded training response is 10,224 tokens against a 12,288-token trajectory budget. Every failed saved episode reaches the 40-turn limit; the evidence points to wasted actions rather than trajectory-context exhaustion. Per-action truncation is not separately quantified by the frozen metrics, and malformed/no-call outputs remain an additional model limitation.
+   - Actor learning rate remains `1e-6`; gradient norms are finite and nonzero (0.00178–0.82292). Reference KL rises from 0.000489 to 0.04139. Zero PPO clipping/old-policy KL and nearly zero scalar policy loss do not prove frozen weights: this configuration uses one minibatch and one PPO epoch, the actor uses `log_prob.detach()` as its on-policy anchor, and group-centered sequence advantages cancel in the scalar loss while retaining gradients.
+   - Training mean reward increases from 0.2570 over steps 1–20 to 0.3594 over steps 41–63, but training batches differ and the held-out treatment families never improve. This supports a localized execution defect despite some learning elsewhere.
+   - Preprocessing records task family, split, and relative game path and leaves success to the environment. The baseline loads 1,008 training rows and 96 validation rows without filtering any out. Each saved training batch contains 16 distinct tasks with four rollouts each, and those saved training task IDs do not overlap validation IDs. The actual parquet files and game assets are absent from this inspection snapshot, so these checks do not establish full-dataset disjointness.
+
+2. **Changes**
+
+   - `tool_schema/alfworld_case/tools.py`: added the reverse mapping derived from `SCHEMA_NAMES`; `command_for()` now resolves advertised aliases before the existing registry lookup and argument validation. For example, `clean_object({"object": "soapbar 1", "receptacle": "sinkbasin 1"})` becomes `clean soapbar 1 with sinkbasin 1`. Native names remain accepted. Model-visible tool names, history, environment success checks, and argument restrictions retain their existing behavior.
+   - `tool_schema/alfworld_case/tests/test_tools.py`: added six CPU-only regression tests covering all 12 advertised tools, dictionary and JSON-string arguments, legacy native names, invalid arguments and unknown names, episode dispatch/history, and environment-controlled success or failure. A recording environment double verifies the execution boundary without loading a model or real game.
+   - `report.md`: added this diagnosis, change inventory, validation results, and expected effects.
+
+   Validation passed: all six regression tests; Python syntax parsing for all local case files; `bash -n tool_schema/alfworld_case/train.sh`; and a read-only dispatch check of all 337 previously rejected treatment calls in the frozen evidence. All 337 now compile to native commands. This checks command translation, not counterfactual task success.
+
+   The launch script remains unchanged. Static inspection confirms the specified model/data paths, `N_GPUS=4` handling (40 default Ray CPU slots), 63-step budget, evaluations at 0/20/40/60/63, and offline W&B plus train/validation/rollout outputs under `RUN_DIR`. No training or model generation was launched, and no frozen logs or metrics were modified. Full integration execution was unavailable: this inspection environment lacks the parquet/game assets and the Torch/Ray/verl/TextWorld dependencies; the repair adds no runtime dependency.
+
+3. **Expected effect**
+
+   Correctly formed calls to the three advertised treatment tools should stop producing `unknown_tool` and reach the environment. Held-out clean/heat/cool family success should rise above the observed zero baseline, improving `val-core/alfworld_valid_seen/reward/mean@1` and `val-core/alfworld_valid_unseen/reward/mean@1` beyond the frozen final 29.17% and 33.33%. These are expectations for the system's fresh run, not measured post-repair results.
+
+   Successful treatment episodes should reduce the fraction reaching 40 turns and lower average environment turns (`val-aux/.../num_steps/mean@1` and training `num_turns/mean`), with possible reductions in rollout latency. Newly reachable successes should also provide useful GRPO reward variation on these task families. Exploration mistakes, malformed calls, and incorrect appliance use can still fail; the repair removes the demonstrated dispatch barrier without assuming every affected episode will succeed.
*** End Patch"));

steps.message:
The experiment is **unhealthy**: a tool-name mismatch blocked cleaning, heating, and cooling, leaving all three families at 0% held-out success.

Fixed the executor mapping. Six CPU-only regression tests pass. No training was launched or logs modified.

Report: [report.md](/workspace/report.md).
